introduction: Today is the Sunday of the Word of God, and it falls during the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity. Jonah preaches to Nineveh, and the whole city turns back to God. Jesus begins his preaching in Galilee: "The time is fulfilled, and God's Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News." Then he calls four fishermen, and they leave their nets at once. Paul reminds us that the world as we know it is passing away. Let us listen to the Word with hearts ready to change.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Word of God calls us to conversion and unity. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For all Christians, during this Week of Prayer for Christian Unity: that, listening together to the Word of God, we may grow toward the unity Christ desires for his disciples. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who proclaim the Scriptures, readers, catechists, preachers, and teachers: that they may hand on the Word faithfully and with love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For cities and nations in need of conversion: that, like the people of Nineveh, they may turn from violence and injustice to the ways of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are called to leave something behind to follow Jesus: that they may answer generously and without fear. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our parish: that the Bible may be opened and read in our homes, so that the Word of God becomes the light of our daily lives. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Father, you sent your Son to proclaim the Good News of your Kingdom. Make us attentive to your Word, ready to turn back to you, and one in faith and love. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Leaving the nets
reflection.body:
Jonah had already run away from God once. Given a second chance, he walks into Nineveh with a short, blunt message: "In forty days, Nineveh will be overthrown!" What happens next surprises everyone, Jonah most of all: "The people of Nineveh believed God," and the whole city fasts, "from their greatest even to their least." God sees that they turn from their evil way, and he spares them. No one is beyond the reach of his word.

Mark sums up the preaching of Jesus in one sentence: "The time is fulfilled, and God's Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News." To repent is not only to feel sorry. It means to turn around, to change the direction of one's life because something new has arrived.

Then Jesus walks along the shore and sees Simon and Andrew at work. "Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men." Mark's answer is short: "Immediately they left their nets, and followed him." James and John leave even their father in the boat. They do not yet know where Jesus will lead them. They know only that he is worth following.

Paul writes to the Corinthians with the same urgency: "the time is short" and "the mode of this world passes away." He does not mean that marriage, grief, joy, or work no longer matter. He means that none of them is ultimate. Only God is.

On this Sunday of the Word of God, ask yourself what net you are still holding on to. Then open the Gospel of Mark this week, a few verses each day, and let the Word that called the fishermen call you too.
